# 05 — Video Playbook (Script & Storyboard)

## Technical Specifications

### Reels Format (Instagram)
- **Optimal duration**: 15-30 seconds (sweet spot for reach)
- **Max recommended duration**: 60 seconds
- **Aspect ratio**: 9:16 (vertical)
- **Resolution**: 1080x1920 px
- **Text safe zone**: avoid top 250px (username) and bottom 400px (CTA/comments)
- **Subtitles**: always. 70%+ watch without sound
- **Cover**: clear frame with readable text for the feed

### TikTok Format
- **Optimal duration**: 15-45 seconds
- **Max recommended duration**: 60 seconds (up to 3 min possible but not recommended for this content type)
- **Aspect ratio**: 9:16 (vertical)
- **Resolution**: 1080x1920 px
- **Text safe zone**: similar to Reels — avoid top and bottom
- **Subtitles**: always
- **Trending sounds**: use when relevant to the content (don't force it)

### Cross-posting Reels ↔ TikTok
- **Yes**: the same video can go on both platforms
- **No**: don't post with TikTok watermark on Instagram (and vice versa)
- **Adjustments**:
  - TikTok: can be slightly more informal, more trend-driven
  - Reels: slightly more polished, fewer ephemeral trends
  - Subtitles must be repositioned for each platform's safe zone

---

## The Complete Script Format

Every [your brand] video script includes 5 layers of information:

### 1. VISUAL (what you see)
- Framing: close-up, medium shot, wide shot, detail shot
- Speaker's facial expressions (crucial for infotainment)
- Props: physical objects used in the scene (pile of resumes, laptop, phone)
- Overlaid graphics, animations
- Transitions: hard cut, zoom, swipe

### 2. AUDIO (what you hear — exact dialogue)
- The word-for-word text spoken by the speaker
- Tone of voice: specific cues (ironic, serious, surprised, exasperated)
- Pacing: fast, pause, emphasis on keywords

### 3. ON-SCREEN TEXT (overlaid text)
- Text that appears on screen
- Position: top, center, bottom
- Font: consistent with brand (bold, sans-serif)
- Timing: when it appears and disappears

### 4. DIRECTING (production notes)
- Cuts: where to cut between scenes
- Zoom: zoom in for emphasis, zoom out for context
- Editing pace: fast (cuts every 2-3 seconds to maintain attention)
- Special transitions (if needed)

### 5. MUSIC/SFX (background audio)
- Music: trending audio, beat, strategic silence
- SFX: impact sounds, "ding", comedic sound, dramatic sound
- Volume: low under speech, high during non-speech moments

---

## The Hook in the First 3 Seconds

### Why the First 3 Seconds Are Everything
The viewer decides whether to keep watching in 1-3 seconds. If the hook doesn't work, everything else is wasted. Initial watch time determines algorithmic distribution.

### 5 Video Hook Techniques

**Technique 1: Visual Pattern Interrupt**
An unexpected visual element that breaks the feed scroll.
- Sudden movement (jumping up, turning around, slamming something on the desk)
- Strong facial expression (shock, exasperation, huge smile)
- Out-of-context object (enormous pile of papers, absurd sign, countdown)
- Unexpected color/lighting

**Technique 2: Curiosity-Driven Opening Line**
The first sentence must create an "open loop" the viewer wants to close.
- "You'll never guess what our ATS did yesterday"
- "The best candidate was in the one resume I hadn't read"
- "I have a confession: I don't read all the resumes"

**Technique 3: Pre-emptive On-Screen Text**
Text appears BEFORE the speaker starts talking, building anticipation.
- "200 resumes. 3 hours. Zero candidates lost."
- "POV: you're an HR on Monday morning"
- "Manual screening in 2026?"

**Technique 4: Direct-to-Camera Question**
The speaker looks at the camera and asks a question that immediately engages.
- "How many resumes did you read this week?"
- "Do you know how many candidates your ATS rejected without you knowing?"
- "Have you ever wondered why you can't find the right candidates?"

**Technique 5: "If..." Scenario**
Start with an "if" the target audience can't ignore.
- "If you've also spent 3 weeks on 200 resumes, this video is for you"
- "If your CEO has ever told you 'how long does it take?', keep watching"
- "If you think manual screening is the only option... sit down"

---

## The Infotainment Style in Video

### The Emotional Arc

```
SETUP (0-5s)        → Frustration/Recognition
                      "The viewer thinks: oh god, that's me"

DEVELOPMENT (5-15s) → Ironic Escalation
                      "The situation gets worse. The absurdity grows"

PAYOFF (15-25s)     → Smart Solution / Plot twist
                      "The viewer thinks: oh, there's a better way"

CTA (25-30s)        → Soft Call to Action
                      "Follow us / Link in bio / Save for later"
```

### The Viewer Should Think:
1. **"Oh god, that's me"** → shares out of solidarity
2. **"I'm smarter than that"** → shares for positioning
3. **"I need to show this to [name]"** → shares for connection
4. **"I didn't know that"** → saves for later

### Performance Guidelines for Founders

**Marta (primary video speaker)**:
- Look at the camera as if talking to a colleague, not an audience
- Natural expressions, not rehearsed
- Short pauses for emphasis (1-2 seconds of silence = extremely powerful)
- Ironic smirk > forced laugh
- Hands visible (natural Italian gesturing)
- Minor mistakes are fine: imperfection is authentic

**Michele (secondary speaker, tech focus)**:
- Calmer but enthusiastic tone
- Show the screen when explaining the technology
- "Watch what happens when..." + real demo
- Genuine excitement about the technology comes through

---

## The 6 Video Templates

### VS1 — The HR POV (V1)

**Use**: everyday situation from the HR perspective.
**Pillar**: 3 (HR in the Trenches)
**Duration**: 15-25 seconds
**Speaker**: Marta

```
[0-2s]
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} at desk, {{EMOTION}} expression
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "POV: {{SITUATION}}"
SFX: notification / alarm / ding sound

[2-7s]
AUDIO: "{{SETUP_LINE}}" (tone: {{TONE}})
VISUAL: {{ACTION}} (opening laptop, looking at screen, sighing)
DIRECTING: close-up, fixed camera

[7-15s]
AUDIO: "{{DEVELOPMENT}}" (tone: escalation)
VISUAL: {{REACTIONS}} (exasperated expressions, gestures)
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{IRONIC_DETAIL}}"
DIRECTING: quick cuts between 2-3 angles

[15-22s]
AUDIO: "{{CLOSING}}" (tone: resigned or ironic)
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} looks at camera with {{FINAL_EXPRESSION}}
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{MESSAGE}}"
MUSIC: trending audio fade in

[22-25s]
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "Follow us for part 2" / "{{CTA}}"
VISUAL: small [your brand] logo at the bottom
```

### VS2 — The Visual Comparison (V2)

**Use**: before vs after, old way vs new way.
**Pillar**: 2 (Hiring Done Right), 4 ([your brand])
**Duration**: 20-30 seconds
**Speaker**: Marta or Michele

```
[0-3s]
VISUAL: split screen / wipe transition
ON-SCREEN TEXT (left): "{{BEFORE_LABEL}}"
ON-SCREEN TEXT (right): "{{AFTER_LABEL}}"
SFX: VS / transition sound

[3-12s] — "BEFORE" SIDE
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} frustrated, at desk with piles of papers
AUDIO: "{{BEFORE_DESCRIPTION}}" (tone: slow, heavy)
ON-SCREEN TEXT:
  "{{NEGATIVE_METRIC_1}}"
  "{{NEGATIVE_METRIC_2}}"
DIRECTING: slightly tilted framing, desaturated colors

[12-22s] — "AFTER" SIDE
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} relaxed, at laptop, [your brand] screen
AUDIO: "{{AFTER_DESCRIPTION}}" (tone: light, fast)
ON-SCREEN TEXT:
  "{{POSITIVE_METRIC_1}}"
  "{{POSITIVE_METRIC_2}}"
DIRECTING: straight framing, vivid colors
MUSIC: upbeat beat

[22-28s]
VISUAL: full screen, {{SPEAKER}} smiles at camera
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{FINAL_MESSAGE}}"
AUDIO: "{{CLOSING_PUNCHLINE}}"

[28-30s]
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "Link in bio" + [your brand] logo
```

### VS3 — The Bombshell Stat (V3)

**Use**: a surprising data point with reaction.
**Pillar**: 1 (The Future of HR), 2 (Hiring Done Right)
**Duration**: 15-20 seconds
**Speaker**: Marta or Michele

```
[0-2s]
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} looks at a "sheet/screen" off-camera, surprised expression
ON-SCREEN TEXT (large, centered): "{{STAT}}"
SFX: impact / boom sound

[2-8s]
AUDIO: "{{EXPLANATION}}" (tone: surprised then analytical)
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} talks to camera
ON-SCREEN TEXT: animated keywords appearing

[8-15s]
AUDIO: "{{IMPLICATION_FOR_TARGET}}" (tone: direct)
VISUAL: close-up, serious
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{BRIEF_TAKEAWAY}}"

[15-18s]
AUDIO: "{{CTA_OR_QUESTION}}"
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "Follow us for more HR data"
VISUAL: [your brand] logo
```

### VS4 — The Mini-Lesson (V4)

**Use**: 3 quick tips in under 30 seconds.
**Pillar**: 2 (Hiring Done Right)
**Duration**: 20-30 seconds
**Speaker**: Marta or Michele

```
[0-3s]
AUDIO: "{{QUICK_HOOK}}" (e.g.: "3 screening mistakes that cost you candidates")
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} holds up 3 fingers / uses prop
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{TITLE}}"

[3-10s]
AUDIO: "First: {{TIP_1}}" (tone: decisive)
VISUAL: "1" gesture + animated graphic
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "1. {{KEYWORD_1}}"
DIRECTING: hard cut to point 2

[10-17s]
AUDIO: "Second: {{TIP_2}}"
VISUAL: "2" gesture + graphic
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "2. {{KEYWORD_2}}"
DIRECTING: hard cut to point 3

[17-24s]
AUDIO: "Third: {{TIP_3}}"
VISUAL: "3" gesture + graphic
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "3. {{KEYWORD_3}}"

[24-30s]
AUDIO: "{{RESULT_IF_YOU_APPLY}}"
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} smiles, points downward
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "Save for later"
MUSIC: closing beat
```

### VS5 — The Comedy Sketch (V5)

**Use**: acted-out skit with 1-2 characters.
**Pillar**: 3 (HR in the Trenches)
**Duration**: 25-45 seconds
**Speaker**: Marta (+ optional second actor for CEO/hiring manager)

```
[0-3s] — INTRO
VISUAL: {{OFFICE_SETTING}}
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{SITUATION_TITLE}}"
SFX: office sound / notification
DIRECTING: quick establishing shot

[3-12s] — SETUP
{{CHARACTER_1}} ({{ROLE}}): "{{LINE_1}}"
{{CHARACTER_2}} ({{ROLE}}): "{{RESPONSE_1}}"
VISUAL: quick shot/reverse shot
DIRECTING: fast cuts, handheld camera for dynamism

[12-22s] — ESCALATION
The absurdity grows:
{{CHARACTER_1}}: "{{ESCALATION_LINE}}"
{{CHARACTER_2}}: "{{EXASPERATED_REACTION}}"
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{IRONIC_COMMENT}}"
DIRECTING: zoom in on the reaction

[22-32s] — PUNCHLINE
{{CHARACTER_2}}: "{{PUNCHLINE}}"
VISUAL: expression breaking the fourth wall (looks at camera)
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{KEY_MESSAGE}}"
SFX: comedic sound / record scratch / dramatic silence

[32-38s] — CLOSING
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} smiles at camera
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{CTA}}" + [your brand] logo
MUSIC: trending audio
```

### VS6 — Everyday Situation + Plot Twist (V6)

**Use**: the SIGNATURE [your brand] format. Frustration → escalation → twist.
**Pillar**: 3 (HR in the Trenches) + 4 ([your brand] in Action)
**Duration**: 20-30 seconds
**Speaker**: Marta

```
[0-2s] — HOOK (Pattern Interrupt)
VISUAL: {{VISUAL_PATTERN_INTERRUPT}}
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{HOOK_LARGE_TEXT}}"
SFX: {{IMPACT_SOUND}}
DIRECTING: jump cut or quick zoom

[2-8s] — SETUP (The Frustration)
AUDIO: "{{FRUSTRATION_DESCRIPTION}}" (tone: resigned/exasperated)
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} lives the situation — natural expressions
ON-SCREEN TEXT: {{SITUATION_DETAIL}}
MUSIC: slow beat or none
DIRECTING: fixed camera, close-up

[8-15s] — ESCALATION (It Gets Worse)
AUDIO: "{{SITUATION_GETS_WORSE}}" (tone: crescendo)
VISUAL: {{EXASPERATED_REACTIONS}} — face, gestures, eyes to the ceiling
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{IRONIC_COMMENT}}"
DIRECTING: fast cuts, zoom in/out

[15-22s] — PLOT TWIST (The Turnaround)
AUDIO: "{{TWIST_LINE}}" (tone: sharp shift — from exasperated to confident/smiling)
VISUAL: sharp expression change. {{SPEAKER}} opens laptop / shows something
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{TWIST_MESSAGE}}"
MUSIC: switch to upbeat beat
SFX: positive sound (ding / whoosh)
DIRECTING: creative transition (wipe, zoom, flash)

[22-28s] — CLOSING
AUDIO: "{{FINAL_PUNCHLINE}}" (tone: satisfied/ironic)
VISUAL: {{SPEAKER}} looks at camera with a knowing smile
ON-SCREEN TEXT: "{{CTA}}" + small [your brand] logo
MUSIC: fade out
```

## Video Pre-Production Checklist

### Before Recording
- [ ] Is the script complete (VISUAL + AUDIO + ON-SCREEN TEXT + DIRECTING + MUSIC)?
- [ ] Does the hook capture attention in the first 2-3 seconds?
- [ ] Has the script been read out loud (real-time timing)?
- [ ] Is the duration within optimal range (15-30s)?
- [ ] Are subtitles planned?
- [ ] Is the tone infotainment (not corporate)?
- [ ] Is the recording environment ready (lighting, background, audio)?

### During Recording
- [ ] Is the speaker looking at the camera (not the screen)?
- [ ] Are facial expressions natural and visible?
- [ ] Is the speaking pace energetic (not monotonous)?
- [ ] Record 2-3 takes per segment (options for editing)?
- [ ] Clean audio (no background noise)?

### In Post-Production
- [ ] Fast cuts (every 2-4 seconds) to maintain attention?
- [ ] Subtitles added and within the safe zone?
- [ ] On-screen text readable and well-positioned?
- [ ] Music/SFX at proper volume (under speech)?
- [ ] [your brand] logo present but not intrusive?
- [ ] Instagram feed cover (clear frame with text)?
- [ ] No watermarks from other platforms?

### Before Publishing
- [ ] Does the video work WITHOUT audio (subtitles + visuals only)?
- [ ] Does the hook work in the feed (do the first 2 frames capture attention)?
- [ ] Is the caption ready (short, with CTA and hashtags)?
- [ ] Hashtags: 5-10 relevant ones (not too many)?
- [ ] Optimal posting time (morning 8-9 AM or lunch 12-1 PM)?

---

## Cross-Platform Notes

| Aspect | Instagram Reels | TikTok |
|--------|----------------|--------|
| **Tone** | Slightly more polished | More spontaneous and raw |
| **Audio** | IG trending audio | Native TikTok sounds |
| **Hashtags** | 5-8 in the caption | 3-5 in the caption |
| **CTA** | "Link in bio" | "Link in bio" / pinned comment |
| **Duration sweet spot** | 15-25 seconds | 15-45 seconds |
| **Posting time** | 8:00-9:00 AM or 12:00-1:00 PM CET | 12:00-2:00 PM or 6:00-8:00 PM CET |
| **Frequency** | 3-4 Reels/week | 3-5 TikToks/week |

# MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson) — YouTube Expert Profile

## Profile
- **Who he is**: Jimmy Donaldson, known as MrBeast, is the biggest creator in YouTube history. He started uploading videos in 2012 at age 13, spending years studying the algorithm and virality. He built a media empire (Beast Industries) that includes Feastables (snacks), Beast Burger, and the fintech app Step. Forbes has valued him at over $1 billion. In 2026 he is evolving toward more narrative and emotional content, with character arcs and longer formats.
- **YouTube subscribers**: ~467 million (main channel), nearly 1 billion total followers across all platforms
- **Total views**: over 50 billion views
- **Specialization**: extreme-scale production, retention, thumbnails, packaging, total reinvestment of revenue into content
- **Channel**: MrBeast

## Core Philosophy

1. **Total reinvestment**: "I've reinvested everything to the point of stupidity." 95-98% of earnings are reinvested in production. Higher budgets = more impressive productions = larger audience = higher revenue = even bigger budgets. A virtuous cycle.
2. **Quality > quantity**: a single video with 5 million views is more valuable than 100 videos with 50,000 views each. Better to invest in a few excellent videos than to produce many mediocre ones.
3. **The best YOUTUBE video, not the best video period**: "Your goal is to make the best YOUTUBE videos possible. Not the best produced videos... the best YOUTUBE videos." Production serves YouTube, not the other way around.
4. **Obsession with the first seconds**: the first 3-5 seconds decide everything. Always open with an extreme action or a statement that creates immediate tension.
5. **Continuous evolution**: in 2026 MrBeast acknowledged that audiences have become "numb" to spectacles. The new frontier is emotional depth, narrative arcs, and character development.

## Frameworks and Methodologies

### Thumbnail Strategy
- **High-contrast colors**: bright yellows, intense reds, vivid blues that stand out against YouTube's white interface
- **The 0-2 word rule**: thumbnails with the most views have 0 or at most 2 words
- **One face, strong emotion**: one person as the primary focus with a happy/excited expression
- **The thumbnail determines success**: it can mean tens of millions of views difference. MrBeast tests thumbnails before even filming the video

### Retention Editing
- High-impact sound effects, rapid cuts, zero pauses
- Every second must justify its existence in the video
- Constant pattern interrupts to maintain attention
- Narrative structure with rising tension

### Global Scalability
- Videos available in 40+ languages
- Professional dubbing and subtitles for every market
- Content designed to be universally understandable

### Iterative Production
- Every video is analyzed in minute detail post-publication
- Continuous A/B testing on thumbnails and titles
- Dedicated team for retention curve analysis

## Hook and Retention Techniques

- **Extreme hook**: open with the most spectacular action or the strongest promise of the video
- **Constant escalation**: every segment must surpass the previous one in intensity
- **Eliminate "dead spots"**: second-by-second analysis of the retention curve to cut every moment of drop-off
- **Internal cliff-hangers**: create micro-suspense between segments
- **Visible payoff**: immediately show what will happen (the prize, the challenge) to build anticipation
- **End screen with 70-80% retention**: the video must maintain high attention until the very last second

## Memorable Quotes and Concepts

1. **"I've reinvested everything to the point of stupidity."** — The total reinvestment philosophy that built the MrBeast empire. Every dollar earned goes back into production.
2. **"Your goal is to make the best YOUTUBE videos possible. Not the best produced videos."** — From the internal production guide: the YouTube format comes before cinematic quality.
3. **"A single video with 5 million views is more valuable than 100 videos with 50,000 views each."** — Quality beats quantity, always.
4. **"The thumbnail is the most important thing. It can mean tens of millions of views difference."** — Packaging is everything: the best video in the world fails with the wrong thumbnail.
5. **"The audience has become numb to spectacles."** (2026) — The new frontier is emotion, not spectacle. Narrative arcs and emotional depth are the future.

## How to Apply to Your Brand

### Reinvesting in Content
Even with limited budgets, the principle holds: dedicate a fixed percentage of content-generated revenue to producing your next piece of content. If a tutorial video generates leads, invest in a better video. Example: HubSpot consistently reinvests in the quality of its educational videos, raising the bar every quarter.

### Thumbnail-First Thinking
Before producing a video, ask yourself: "What's the thumbnail?" If you can't picture an image that generates clicks, the concept needs to be reworked. For a B2B/SaaS brand, this means: large numbers prominently displayed, a human face with emotion, color contrast with the feed.

### The First 3 Seconds
In [your brand]'s videos, open with the most surprising data point or the most provocative question. Never with the logo. Never with "Hi, today we're talking about..." Example: Notion opens its videos with the final result, then explains how to get there.

### Quality Over Quantity
Better 2 exceptional videos per month than 8 mediocre ones. Every video should be designed to be the best possible on that topic on YouTube. Focus resources, time, and creativity.

### Post-Publication Analysis
After every video, analyze the retention curve second by second. Where does it drop? Why? Use that data to improve the next video. This is the continuous improvement cycle that made MrBeast number one.

## Key Resources
- **YouTube Channel**: [youtube.com/@MrBeast](https://youtube.com/@MrBeast)
- **Courses**: no public courses, but the "MrBeast Production Guide" (leaked) has become study material for creators
- **Books**: no published books
- **Podcast/Other**: in-depth interviews with Colin and Samir, Joe Rogan, Lex Fridman; Beast Industries manages multiple lines of business

# Jenny Hoyos — YouTube Expert Profile

## Profile
- **Who she is**: An American creator of Colombian origin, graduated from Florida International University, considered the "queen of YouTube Shorts". At just 20 years old she built one of the most successful Shorts channels in the world, reaching 1.5 million subscribers with only 97 Shorts. Her videos regularly accumulate 10+ million views each. She started with a specific niche (finance for teenagers), reaching 100K subscribers, then made a strategic pivot toward broader content (saving and money hacks) that brought her to 3M+ subscribers. YouTube itself chose her as an official case study for Shorts.
- **YouTube subscribers**: ~10,100,000
- **Total views**: ~3 billion
- **Specialization**: YouTube Shorts, short-form video strategy, storytelling in short format, viral content, retention optimization
- **Channel**: Jenny Hoyos

## Core Philosophy
1. **You have 1 second to capture attention**: in short formats there's no "warm-up phase". The hook must be immediate, visual, and understandable even without audio.
2. **90% retention is the minimum**: a good Short must retain 90%+ of viewers until the end. Below this threshold, the algorithm won't push the content.
3. **Storytelling > Information**: people don't share information, they share stories. Even a 30-second video needs a complete narrative arc.
4. **The ending determines everything**: viewers judge the video based on the emotion they feel at the end. A weak ending ruins all the work done before.
5. **Less is more**: better 1 perfect Short per month than 30 mediocre ones. Script quality is more important than publishing frequency.

## Frameworks and Methodologies

### BUTS (But-So) Storytelling Method
A storytelling method for maintaining narrative tension in short videos:
- Every Short follows a structure of chained conflicts using "but" and "so"
- Example: "I bought a $1 sandwich... BUT it tasted like nothing... SO I added the secret ingredients... BUT the total cost went up to $3... SO I compared it with the original $8 one..."
- Every "but" introduces a new conflict, every "so" a reaction — the viewer can't stop watching because the story never stops

### Foreshadowing Hook
An opening technique that builds expectation:
- The first second hints at the final result/comparison without revealing it
- Example: "Chick-fil-A has the best chicken sandwich, but I'm not paying $6. So I make it for $1 and then compare them."
- The viewer MUST watch to the end to see the comparison result

### Content Buckets Strategy
A system for organizing content into recognizable thematic series:
- Each "bucket" is a recurring series (e.g., "$1 fast food items", "finding gold in cheap items")
- When a viewer enjoys a video from a series, they watch all the others in the same series
- Buckets create expectation and recognition: the viewer knows what to expect and comes back for it

### Power Words System
Words that generate instant clicks and views:
- **Curiosity**: "secret", "hidden", "nobody knows"
- **Urgency**: "banned", "last time", "before it disappears"
- **Value**: "free", "$1", "half price"
- **Exclusivity**: "for the first time", "never seen", "sneak peek"
- These words must appear in the first 3 seconds, in the title, or in the text overlay

### Pivot Strategy (Niche > Mainstream)
A 2-phase growth strategy:
1. **Phase 1 — Niche**: start with a specific and less competitive topic to build a base of loyal subscribers (e.g., finance for teenagers)
2. **Phase 2 — Expansion**: once you've reached critical mass, broaden the topic while keeping the style and format (e.g., from "teen finance" to "saving for everyone")

## Hook and Retention Techniques
- **Silent visual hook**: the first frame must communicate the content even without audio. Clear text overlay, impactful images, immediate action
- **1 second rule**: if the viewer can't understand the video's topic within 1 second, they'll swipe. No intro, no greetings, no context — immediate action
- **Transitions as narrative engine**: transitions aren't decorative, they're narrative. Every transition moves the story forward and maintains the pace
- **Continuous conflict**: never leave a moment of "calm" in the video. Every 3-5 seconds something new must happen
- **High emotional intensity ending**: the video must end at the moment of maximum emotion. Never close with an "and so..." but with a climax
- **Retention rate as north-star metric**: Jenny obsessively analyzes the retention curve of every video, identifying drop-off points and modifying the structure of subsequent videos accordingly

## Memorable Quotes and Concepts
- **"You have one second to hook someone on Shorts. One. Second."** — On the urgency of the hook
- **"A good hook should be so clear that viewers understand the video even on mute."** — On the accessibility of the visual hook
- **"I aim for 90% retention or higher. Below that, the algorithm won't push your content."** — On the retention threshold
- **"Use 'but' and 'so' to keep the story moving. Never let the viewer feel like the story is over."** — On the BUTS method
- **"The viewer decides how they felt about the video based on the intensity of the emotion at the end."** — On the importance of the ending

## How to Apply to Your Brand
- **Use the BUTS method for every Short**: even a 30-second B2B video can follow the "but/so" structure. Example: "[Common industry problem]... BUT most solutions cost too much... SO we tried a different approach... BUT the results surprised us..."
- **Create recognizable Content Buckets**: define 3-4 recurring series for [your brand]'s Shorts channel. Example: "Industry myths in 30 seconds", "Tool of the week", "Before and after". Each series becomes a recurring appointment for the audience.
- **Apply the first-second rule**: watch your Short without audio. If you can't understand the topic in 1 second, redo it. Add clear text overlay and an impactful image in the first frame.
- **Aim for 90% retention**: if your Shorts have retention below 70%, the problem is in the script, not in the production. Use the BUTS method to add narrative tension.
- **Start from the niche, then expand**: don't try to speak to everyone. A SaaS brand could start with Shorts on a single use case, build a base, and then expand to broader industry topics.
